verdict.rationale: React's own React Compiler is a build-time tool with a debugging guide that separates compile-time errors, which stop the build, from runtime issues (react-docs-18). It also documents safely skipping code that breaks the Rules of React (react-docs-43), and the official eslint-plugin-react-hooks catches severe bugs early (react-docs-19). React itself ships no dev server; it defers to third-party build tools like Vite (react-docs-22), and the evidence never shows how clear or actionable the error messages are. missing for 10: a first-party dev server with error overlays, examples or documentation of error message content and actionability, independent or hands-on corroboration of error quality.
